2) Implementation of missing-annotation auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING / REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE / REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts: - Annotated to this story and requirements: * @story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-MISSING - This rule supports auto-fixing missing @story annotations per Story 008.0 auto-fix behavior. * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE - Auto-fix behavior only inserts @story annotation JSDoc comments and never changes executable or runtime code. * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE - Auto-fix inserts a minimal placeholder JSDoc in a way that preserves existing surrounding formatting and structure. - meta: meta: { type: "problem", docs: { description: "Require @story annotations on functions and auto-fix missing annotations where possible", recommended: "error" }, hasSuggestions: true, fixable: "code", ... } - src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts: - Defines a simple built-in template used for auto-fix: const STORY_PATH = "docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md"; const ANNOTATION = `/** @story ${STORY_PATH} */`; - reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?): - First checks hasStoryAnnotation(...) to avoid duplicate or unsafe fixes. - Resolves an insertion target with resolveTargetNode(...). - Reports with both fix and suggestion: context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), suggest: [ { desc: `Add JSDoc @story annotation for function '${name}', e.g., ${ANNOTATION}`, fix: createAddStoryFix(resolvedTarget), }, ], }); - Wrapped in try/catch to avoid crashing ESLint on edge cases. - reportMethod(...) behaves analogously for methods using createMethodFix. - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts: - createAddStoryFix(target): - Computes a safe start position using either the target's export parent or its own range, then: return fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([start, start], `${ANNOTATION}\n`); - createMethodFix(node): - Similar range logic but inserts with trailing indentation: return fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([start, start], `${ANNOTATION}\n `); - These fixers: - Only insert a comment line; they do not modify function bodies or runtime code. - Preserve surrounding indentation and code structure aside from adding the annotation line. - Match the before/after examples asserted in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts for all supported node types.
3) Implementation of format auto-fix (REQ-AUTOFIX-FORMAT / REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE / REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE) - src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts: - createStoryFix(context, comment, fixed): - Obtains original comment text via context.getSourceCode().getText(comment). - Locates "@story" and then the path value using a regex. - If the tag or value range cannot be determined, returns null: if (tagIndex === TAG_NOT_FOUND_INDEX) return null; if (!valueMatch || valueMatch.index === undefined) return null; - Computes fixRange to cover only the path substring, and returns a closure producing: fixer.replaceTextRange(fixRange, fixed); - reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(context, comment, collapsed, fixed): - Calls createStoryFix(...). - If no safe fixFactory is produced, falls back to plain reportInvalidStoryFormat(...), i.e. validation only. - Otherwise calls context.report with fix: fixFactory(). - This behavior is explicitly documented as: // @req REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE - Fall back to reporting without fix when safe fix cannot be created - validateStoryAnnotation(context, comment, rawValue, options): - Normalizes the path, checks against pathPattern. - If pattern fails but there is no internal whitespace, computes fixed = getFixedStoryPath(collapsed). - If fixed exists and pathPattern.test(fixed) is true, it calls reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix(...). - Otherwise reports without fix. - meta.fixable: /** * This rule's fixable support is limited to safe @story path suffix normalization per Story 008.0. * Fixes are limited strictly to adjusting the suffix portion of the @story path (e.g., adding * `.md` or `.story.md`), preserving all other comment text and whitespace exactly as written. * * @story docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE * @req REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE */ fixable: "code", - This logic exactly matches the tested scenarios in auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts where only suffixes are changed and everything else (including comment style) is preserved.
4) Error handling and safety for unfixable or ambiguous cases (Error Handling AC, REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE) - For missing @story annotations: - hasStoryAnnotation(...) performs multiple heuristics to detect existing annotations (JSDoc, leading comments, fallback text windows, parent chain) and short-circuits before calling fixers when an annotation is already present. - reportMissing and reportMethod are wrapped in try/catch, so unexpected parsing or source issues cause the rule to noop rather than throw. - For format fixes: - If @story tag not found or value range is ambiguous, createStoryFix returns null and no fix is attached. - If getFixedStoryPath cannot produce a valid, pattern-conforming path, the rule reports the error without proposing a fix.
5) Documentation of auto-fix capabilities (Documentation AC) - user-docs/api-reference.md, rule traceability/require-story-annotation: "When run with `--fix`, the rule inserts a single-line placeholder JSDoc `@story` annotation above missing functions, methods, TypeScript declare functions, and interface method signatures using a built-in template aligned with Story 008.0. This template is currently fixed but structured for future configurability, and fixes are strictly limited to adding this placeholder annotation without altering the function body or changing any runtime behavior." - user-docs/api-reference.md, rule traceability/valid-annotation-format: "When run with `--fix`, the rule limits changes to safe `@story` path suffix normalization only—for example, adding `.md` when the path ends with `.story`, or adding `.story.md` when the base path has no extension—using targeted replacements implemented in the `getFixedStoryPath` and `reportInvalidStoryFormatWithFix` helpers. It does not change directories, infer new story names, or modify any surrounding comment text or whitespace, in line with Story 008.0; more advanced path normalization strategies and selective toggles to enable or disable specific auto-fix behaviors are not yet implemented." - These docs align with the behavior in the code and tests and explicitly reference Story 008.0.
6) Scope of not-yet-implemented requirements - The story itself marks these as not yet implemented: - REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE: configurable annotation templates. - REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE: fine-grained toggles for which fix types to enable. - The current implementation does not claim to support these; configuration is limited to standard ESLint rule enable/disable and the fixed built-in template, matching the story's description of the current iteration.
Overall, the implementation, tests, and documentation together show that all in-scope acceptance criteria and implemented requirements for Story 008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX are satisfied.
traceability.notes:
All in-scope acceptance criteria for docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md are fully implemented.
• Core functionality and integration: ESLint's --fix mode is supported via fixable rules `traceability/require-story-annotation` and `traceability/valid-annotation-format`. The dedicated test file `tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts` is explicitly tied to this story and verifies correct before/after behavior for missing @story annotations on multiple function/method shapes and for simple @story path suffix normalization. These tests pass in the full Jest run, confirming correct integration with the ESLint RuleTester and toolchain.
• Safety, formatting, and error handling: For missing @story, the plugin only inserts a single-line JSDoc comment using a conservative, fixed template and never alters function bodies or executable code, satisfying REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE and REQ-AUTOFIX-PRESERVE. It checks for existing annotations and uses try/catch to avoid crashes. For format fixes, the rule computes and replaces only the story path substring within an existing comment, and bails out to a non-fixing error when the tag/value cannot be reliably located or a safe, pattern-conforming suffix cannot be derived. This ensures that ambiguous or unsafe cases are reported but not auto-fixed, as required.
• User experience and consistency: The auto-fix behavior is deterministic across a clear, documented set of code patterns (various function/method forms and comment-based @story paths). The tests exercise each scenario with explicit expected output, showing consistent and predictable fixes. Already-correct annotations are left unchanged, which the tests also confirm.
• Documentation: user-docs/api-reference.md documents what `--fix` does for both rules, including the template behavior for missing @story and the suffix-only normalization for @story paths, and states the safety constraints (no runtime changes, no directory or name inference). This aligns exactly with the implementation and with the story’s description of current capabilities.
• Out-of-scope features: REQ-AUTOFIX-TEMPLATE and REQ-AUTOFIX-SELECTIVE are explicitly marked as "Not yet implemented" in the story and are not promised by the current release. The implementation reflects this: the template is fixed in code, and there are no extra toggles beyond normal ESLint configuration. Given the story text, this is the expected state for this iteration.
Because the implemented behavior, passing tests, and documentation collectively satisfy the checked acceptance criteria and all marked-as-implemented requirements for Story 008.0, the assessment status is PASSED.
